France.name: Mortier
France.biography: Edouard Mortier - steady, imperturbable, and universally liked - one of the few marshals who has made no enemies in the army.

France.name: Grouchy
France.biography: Emmanuel de Grouchy - precise, methodical, France's finest cavalry tactician after Murat. Executes his orders to the letter; expect nothing beyond them.

France.name: Suchet
France.biography: Louis-Gabriel Suchet - the best administrator in the army. Provinces prosper under his hand; his troops are always paid, always fed.

France.name: Oudinot
France.biography: Nicolas Oudinot - the grenadier's grenadier, collector of thirty-four wounds. Leads from the front because he knows no other place.

France.name: Augereau
France.biography: Pierre Augereau - the brawler of Castiglione, a duelist risen from the gutters of Paris. Past his best years, still dangerous in a fight.

France.name: Marmont
France.biography: Auguste Marmont - artillery savant, companion of the Emperor's youth, and the most nakedly ambitious officer in France.

France.name: Senarmont
France.biography: Alexandre de Senarmont - master of the massed battery, who rolls the guns forward to shatter a line at the decisive hour. France's artillery is the finest in Europe, and her gunners the cheapest to raise.

Austria.name: Schwarzenberg
Austria.biography: Karl Philipp zu Schwarzenberg - the diplomat-soldier. Careful, patient, and impossible to provoke into a battle he has not already won.

Austria.name: Hiller
Austria.biography: Johann von Hiller - methodical, quarrelsome, and exact. Holds whatever he is told to hold, and files a protest afterward.

Austria.name: Liechtenstein
Austria.biography: Johann von Liechtenstein - the cavalry prince. Charges first, negotiates after.

Austria.name: Smola
Austria.biography: Josef Smola - Austria's foremost gunner, a lifelong artillerist who lays a massed battery with a duelist's eye.

Russia.name: Bagration
Russia.biography: Pyotr Bagration - the fiery Georgian, Suvorov's favorite pupil. Give him the rearguard and he becomes a wall; give him the vanguard and he becomes a spear.

Russia.name: Dokhturov
Russia.biography: Dmitry Dokhturov - the unshakeable. Small, ill, half-deaf, and utterly immovable from any post entrusted to him.

Russia.name: Kutaisov
Russia.biography: Alexander Kutaisov - the young prodigy of the Russian guns, brilliant, beloved, and brave to a fault.

Prussia.name: Blucher
Prussia.biography: Gebhard von Blucher - Marshal Forwards. Seventy years of fury on horseback; the only general in Europe who attacks as instinctively as Ney.

Prussia.name: Scharnhorst
Prussia.biography: Gerhard von Scharnhorst - the quiet Hanoverian professor who intends to rebuild the Prussian army from its foundations.

Prussia.name: Yorck
Prussia.biography: Ludwig Yorck - dour, exact, and stiff-necked. Obeys the letter of every order and trusts no one, least of all his superiors.

Prussia.name: Holtzendorff
Prussia.biography: Karl von Holtzendorff - keeper of the King's artillery reserve, methodical and precise where the Prussian line is not.

Britain.name: Wellesley
Britain.biography: Arthur Wellesley - the Sepoy General, home from India with a reputation and a plan. Picks his ground, holds it, and never fights the battle his enemy wants.

Britain.name: Shrapnel
Britain.biography: Henry Shrapnel - Royal Artillery officer whose spherical case-shot bursts above a line and scythes it down; Britain's guns are few but deadly.

Holland.name: Dumonceau
Holland.biography: Jean-Baptiste Dumonceau - a Brussels-born general of the Batavian army; his Dutch division marched with Marmont's corps to the Danube in 1805.

Holland.name: Daendels
Holland.biography: Herman Willem Daendels - patriot of 1795 and the Batavian army's restless organiser; he led the Dutch into Germany in 1806.

Holland.name: Chasse
Holland.biography: David Hendrik Chasse - 'General Bayonet' to the French for his charges in Spain; a Dutch brigadier who never waited to be ordered forward.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Teulie
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Pietro Teulie - Milanese patriot and minister of war; he led the Italian division north with the Grande Armee in 1805 and fell before Kolberg in 1807.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Pino
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Domenico Pino - the Italian army's fighting general; his division stormed in Spain and held at Maloyaroslavets in 1812.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Lechi
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Giuseppe Lechi - a Brescian cavalryman who commanded the Italian division that held Barcelona in 1808.

Switzerland.name: Amey
Switzerland.biography: Francois Pierre Amey - a Swiss officer in French service; he brought the Swiss regiments across the Berezina in 1812.

Bavaria.name: Wrede
Bavaria.biography: Carl Philipp von Wrede - the Bavarian army's field commander from Ulm to Wagram; he led the Bavarians into Russia in 1812 and against Napoleon at Hanau in 1813.

Saxony.name: Thielmann
Saxony.biography: Johann von Thielmann - a Saxon cavalry general; his cuirassiers charged the Great Redoubt at Borodino, and he went over to the allies in 1813.

DuchyOfWarsaw.name: Poniatowski
DuchyOfWarsaw.biography: Jozef Poniatowski - nephew of the last king of Poland and the Duchy's minister of war; he led the Polish corps to Moscow and died at Leipzig a Marshal of France.

DuchyOfWarsaw.name: Dabrowski
DuchyOfWarsaw.biography: Jan Henryk Dabrowski - founder of the Polish Legions in Italy; he raised the Poles of Posen in 1806.

Spain.name: La Romana
Spain.biography: Pedro Caro, Marquis of La Romana - he led the Spanish division lent to Napoleon to Denmark in 1807, and spirited it home aboard British ships in 1808.

Denmark.name: Ewald
Denmark.biography: Johann von Ewald - a Danish general of light troops who hunted Schill's raiders to Stralsund in 1809.

Portugal.name: Gomes Freire
Portugal.biography: Gomes Freire de Andrade - commander of the Portuguese Legion in French service, which marched to Russia in 1812.

Prussia.name: Grawert
Prussia.biography: Julius von Grawert - first commander of the Prussian auxiliary corps that marched with the Grande Armee in 1812.

Austria.title: Revanche
Austria.blurb: What was taken shall be retaken. The court has not forgiven the loss of Bohemia and 1 more.
Austria.author: France

Austria.title: Redeem Italy
Austria.blurb: The priority theater of 1805 - Charles holds the main army in Italy; the losses of Campo Formio and Luneville must be undone.

Austria.title: Primacy in Germany
Austria.blurb: Mack's thrust to the Iller - Bavaria's defection to France must be punished and the German lands held for the Habsburg crown.

Austria.title: The Eastern Question
Austria.blurb: The Porte is failing, and the Habsburg frontier runs where the Turk is weakest. If Italy and Germany are closed to Vienna, the Danube and the Adriatic are not: Albania and Rumelia would make the House of Austria the master of the Balkans before St Petersburg can be.

Prussia.title: The Hanoverian Prize
Prussia.blurb: Napoleon dangles the Electorate at Schoenbrunn; Berlin covets it openly. The buy-Prussia lever.

Prussia.title: Armed Neutrality
Prussia.blurb: North Germany is Prussia's yard - a belligerent marching through it, as at Ansbach, enrages Berlin.

Britain.title: The Low Countries
Britain.blurb: The Scheldt obsession - the invasion coast may not stay in French hands. London will not rest while the bloc holds it.

Britain.title: The Paymaster of Coalitions
Britain.blurb: Pitt's gold - 1.25 million pounds per hundred thousand men, the subsidy conventions of 1805.

Russia.title: Arbiter of Europe
Russia.blurb: Alexander campaigns as the guardian of the European order - the Tsar fights the hegemon while the coalition stands.

Russia.title: The Gulf and the Straits
Russia.blurb: Petersburg is shielded on the Gulf and completed at the Straits - the Tsar's two shores. A design that waits behind the war with France, and wakes the day that war is no longer the Tsar's concern.

Sweden.title: Scourge of the Usurper
Sweden.blurb: Gustav IV's personal anti-Napoleon zeal - the King of Sweden treats the Emperor as a usurper to be unmade.

Ottoman.title: Guard the Straits
Ottoman.blurb: The Porte stays neutral; the Straits are inviolate.

Sardinia.title: The House of Savoy Restored
Sardinia.blurb: The court in Cagliari wants its mainland back.

Denmark.title: Neutrality of the North
Denmark.blurb: Armed neutrality - the fleet is the state.

KingdomOfItaly.title: Risorgimento
KingdomOfItaly.blurb: The dream the vassal wakes with - a free Italian crown gathering the peninsula. Dormant while Milan answers to Paris.

forms.blurb: By the will of the nation and the fortune of arms - the KINGDOM OF ITALY is no more. ITALY stands.

KingdomOfItaly.title: Guard the Peninsula
KingdomOfItaly.blurb: A nation that has just made itself consolidates. The peninsula is gathered; now it is held - and a foreign column crossing it is an insult to a country that exists.

Holland.title: The Seventeen Provinces
Holland.blurb: A free Holland reaching for the Austrian-Netherlands inheritance. Dormant while Amsterdam answers to Paris.

forms.blurb: The inheritance of Burgundy is gathered under one crown - the UNITED NETHERLANDS is proclaimed at Amsterdam.

Holland.title: The Merchants' Peace
Holland.blurb: The counting houses want the sea lanes open and the armies elsewhere. A Netherlands at peace is a Netherlands that trades.

Holland.title: Ostfriesland
Holland.blurb: The Ems coast the Treaty of Fontainebleau gave Louis Bonaparte's kingdom in 1807 - the one province of Holland's own dream its lord can give, once the land is his. Dormant while Amsterdam answers to Paris.

France.name: The Grand Quartier Général
France.says: Berthier's headquarters grown into a true general staff: one more order carried each day.

France.name: The Train des Équipages
France.says: A military train of the state's own wagons, decreed after the Polish winter: a French army in poor or stripped country draws its full supply again - while the Grand Quartier Général stands to run it.

France.name: The Artillery Reserve
France.says: The Guard's reserve batteries and a standard gun park: artillery levies cost 15% less.

France.name: The Anticipated Class
France.date: the senatus-consultes calling the class early, 1806–07
France.says: The Senate calls each year's conscripts before their time: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

France.name: The Berlin Decree
France.says: Every client of the Empire shuts its ports to British goods, whatever its autonomy.

France.name: The Code Abroad
France.date: the Civil Code imposed in Italy (1806), Westphalia (1807) and Warsaw (1808)
France.says: The Civil Code carried into the client states binds them to the Empire: +1 loyalty a turn in every one.

Austria.name: The Corps d'Armée
Austria.says: The Archduke's corps d'armée, the system France has used since 1800, copied at last: one more order carried each day, and the Hofkriegsrat's delays are over - the corps gather as France's do.

Austria.name: The Landwehr
Austria.says: A militia of every able man, raised by imperial patent: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

Austria.name: The Jäger Battalions
Austria.says: Light infantry raised and trained on the French model: infantry recruits muster 10 morale higher.

Austria.name: The New Infantry Regulations
Austria.says: The Archduke's new drill book: a corps that drills recovers 5 more morale.

Austria.name: The Generalissimus
Austria.says: The Archduke placed over the Aulic Council: every levy costs 10% less.

Prussia.name: The General Staff
Prussia.says: Scharnhorst's General Staff, built on the French headquarters that beat Prussia: one more order carried each day.

Prussia.name: The Krümper System
Prussia.says: Men trained in rotation and sent home, a reserve beyond the treaty's limit: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

Prussia.name: The Articles of War
Prussia.says: Flogging abolished and promotion opened to merit: infantry recruits muster 10 morale higher, and - once the General Staff stands - the army is no longer brittle: a lopsided defeat costs what it costs France.

Prussia.name: The Military Reorganisation Commission
Prussia.says: Scharnhorst's commission remakes the army on the French pattern: a corps that drills recovers 5 more morale.

Prussia.name: The Emancipation Edict
Prussia.says: Serfdom ended by edict, and free men answer the levy: infantry recruits cost 10% less.

Russia.name: The Divisional System
Russia.says: Permanent divisions on the French pattern: one more order carried each day, and the columns gather as France's do - the army is no longer slow to concentrate.

Russia.name: Arakcheev's Artillery
Russia.says: Arakcheev's standard guns and parks: artillery levies cost 15% less.

Russia.name: The Opolchenie
Russia.says: The Tsar's militia called up by manifesto: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

Russia.name: The Extraordinary Levy
Russia.says: Serfs taken from the estates by extraordinary levy: infantry recruits cost 20% less and muster 10 morale lower.

Russia.name: The War Ministry under Arakcheev
Russia.says: Arakcheev's ministry drills the army to the letter: a corps that drills recovers 5 more morale.

Britain.name: The Horse Guards Reforms
Britain.says: The Duke of York's reforms at the Horse Guards, a staff to match the French one: one more order carried each day.

Britain.name: The Orders in Council
Britain.says: Neutral trade with the blockaded ports forbidden by Order in Council: a court Britain blockades loses a quarter more of its trade.

Britain.name: The Militia Transfer
Britain.says: Castlereagh draws volunteers from the militia into the line: infantry manpower returns 25% faster, and - once the Horse Guards Reforms stand - the draft is no longer irreplaceable: recruits cost what France's do.

Britain.name: The Commissariat
Britain.says: A Commissariat able to feed an army in the field: fed supply capacity a quarter larger.

Britain.name: Congreve's Rockets
Britain.says: Congreve's rockets beside the guns: artillery levies cost 15% less.

France.name: The Corps System
France.says: The corps march apart and fight together - and eat what the country gives them.

Britain.name: The Line Holds
Britain.says: A small army that cannot be replaced, and a line that does not give way.

Russia.name: Stubborn
Russia.says: Easier to kill than to beat - and slow to gather from the ends of an empire.
Russia.shared_on_purpose: RV-9: Russia and Austria share the flaw France's strength answers - the absence of the corps system - and both cure it by copying it (Russia's divisions, 1806; Austria's corps, 1809).

Austria.name: The Hereditary Lands
Austria.says: Beaten, and back with another army - once Vienna has written the orders.
Austria.shared_on_purpose: RV-9: the one shared clause - see Russia.

Prussia.name: Frederick's Drill
Prussia.says: Frederick's army still attacks as it did at Leuthen, and it breaks all at once.

DuchyOfWarsaw.blurb: Out of Prussia's Polish partition, a Polish state stands again - the DUCHY OF WARSAW is erected.

diplomat.name: Chancery of Warsaw
diplomat.biography: Speaks for a Polish state that exists at a patron's pleasure, and remembers that it did not always.

deck.title: The Commonwealth Restored
deck.blurb: A Duchy is not a kingdom. The old Commonwealth lands lie east - dormant while Warsaw answers to a foreign patron, and a red line for every court that partitioned her.

forms.blurb: The partitions are undone by the fortune of arms - the DUCHY OF WARSAW is no more. The KINGDOM OF POLAND stands.

deck.title: Guard the Vistula
deck.blurb: A country that was erased once holds what it has regathered. A foreign column on the Vistula is not a march - it is a memory.

Normandy.blurb: The old duchy is severed from the French crown - the DUCHY OF NORMANDY is erected.

diplomat.name: Chancery of Rouen
diplomat.biography: A duchy resurrected by France's enemies, and quietly aware of what that makes it.

RomanRepublic.blurb: The temporal power is ended and the tree of liberty planted on the Capitol - the ROMAN REPUBLIC is proclaimed.

diplomat.name: Chancery of the Capitol
diplomat.biography: A consul of the restored Republic, ruling from the city of the Popes and answerable to bayonets.

Ireland.blurb: The risen harp - a French bayonet holds the ring while an Irish republic is proclaimed at Dublin. Erin go bragh.

diplomat.name: Directory of United Irishmen
diplomat.biography: Wolfe Tone's heirs - a directory that owes its republic to a foreign fleet and remembers Bantry Bay, when the wind alone saved England.

deck.title: Erin Free
deck.blurb: A republic born of a naval gamble holds its two provinces against the day the Royal Navy returns. What the sea gave, the sea can take back.

Ney.name: Ney

ability.name: Bravest of the Brave
ability.description: Ney's aggressive leadership inspires devastating attacks

Ney.biography: VI Corps - crossed the Rhine opposite Durlach on September 26. The bravest of the brave leads infantry now; the Cavalry Reserve rides with Murat.

Davout.name: Davout

ability.name: Iron Resolve
ability.description: The iron marshal coils behind his earthworks - patient discipline becomes a hammer-blow when III Corps springs
ability.effect: Each fortified turn builds +1 resolve stack (max 3). His next attack consumes all stacks for +8% each (max +24%). Stacks survive unfortify but clear if he moves or is routed.

Davout.biography: III Corps - crossed the Rhine at Mannheim on September 26. The iron marshal, exacting and incorruptible.

Soult.name: Soult

ability.name: Drillmaster of Boulogne
ability.description: Soult drilled the camps of Boulogne to clockwork - his corps sharpens in a single day
ability.effect: Drill completes in 1 turn (not 2) and never locks him out of your orders

Soult.biography: IV Corps - marching for the Speyer crossing from its Lorraine camps, 10,000 of its best carved away to form the Emperor's Guard. A superb tactician who executes the Emperor's plan to the letter, exactly on the appointed hour.

Lannes.name: Lannes

ability.name: Roland of the Army
ability.description: Lannes marches to the sound of the guns - the second wave that (almost) always comes

Lannes.biography: V Corps - crossed at Kehl on September 25, pressing the Black Forest feint.

Murat.name: Murat

ability.name: First Horseman of Europe
ability.description: When Murat personally breaks an enemy, his cavalry turns the rout into annihilation
ability.effect: +5,000 pursuit casualties when an enemy he defeats is forced to retreat (cavalry, leading the attack)

Murat.biography: The Cavalry Reserve - screening the Black Forest feint while the army wheels north of the Danube.

Bernadotte.name: Bernadotte

ability.name: Eyes on a Crown
ability.description: Bernadotte weighs every order against his own ambitions - the I Corps does not always march
ability.effect: +10% defiance after insisted objections; -15 reinforcement arrival score (a written support order mostly cancels it)

Bernadotte.biography: I Corps at Wuerzburg, marched down from occupied Hanover - standing on allied Bavarian soil across Mack's rear.

Massena.name: Massena

ability.name: Child of Victory
ability.description: Cornered and outnumbered is where Massena fights best

Massena.biography: The Army of Italy on the Adige, facing Archduke Charles - the dear child of victory, chafing on the defensive: set to hold the second front, but itching to throw his corps across the river at the Austrians.

Napoleon.name: Napoleon

ability.name: The Presence
ability.description: His presence on the field was worth forty thousand men - Wellington
ability.effect: Every French corps fighting in the Emperor's province gains +10% attack and defense. Enemy commanders will not attack his army at odds they would accept against any marshal.

Napoleon.biography: Emperor of the French, on the Rhine with the Guard - 10,000 men carved from Soult's own IV Corps, and Soult's corps is drawn up beside them. He left Paris on the 24th of September and the army is across the river; Mack sits at Ulm one march east. The Grande Armee is his instrument; the Empire is his estate; the marshals shine only in his light - or out of it.

Deroy.name: Deroy
Deroy.biography: The Bavarian field army - two divisions under Deroy and Wrede, withdrawn to Wuerzburg rather than submit to Austria, now under French operational direction.

Mack.name: Mack
Mack.biography: The Army of Germany, camped around Ulm on invaded Bavarian soil - quartermaster's plans and paper certainties, deep in hostile country.

ArchdukeCharles.name: ArchdukeCharles

ability.name: Habsburg Resolve
ability.description: Archduke Charles steadies the line with calm under fire

ArchdukeCharles.biography: Austria's main army behind the Adige - the Habsburgs' best soldier, husbanding his strength for the Italian front.

Kutuzov.name: Kutuzov

ability.name: The Old Fox
ability.description: Kutuzov's fighting retreat is his art - chasing him is a half-harvest trap
ability.effect: Pursuit casualties against him halved; retreat-path attrition halved

Kutuzov.biography: The Army of Podolia marching west to join Austria - the one-eyed old fox, weeks away still.

Buxhowden.name: Buxhowden
Buxhowden.biography: The Army of Volhynia, the second echelon - weeks behind Kutuzov on its namesake ground.

Moore.name: Moore

ability.name: Shorncliffe System
ability.description: Moore's recruits arrive drilled - Britain rebuilds quality, not just numbers
ability.effect: Troops he recruits arrive at morale 60 (green conscripts arrive at 40)

Moore.biography: Major-General Sir John Moore, home command at Shorncliffe - trainer of the finest light infantry in Europe.

Brunswick.name: Brunswick
Brunswick.biography: The Duke of Brunswick, Prussia's senior field marshal - the army in home cantonments, armed and neutral.

Hohenlohe.name: Hohenlohe
Hohenlohe.biography: Prince Hohenlohe's corps in Silesia, watching the Russian marches on the tense northern flank.

Armfelt.name: Armfelt
Armfelt.biography: Gustav Mauritz Armfelt, commander of Sweden's Pomeranian expedition - the king's sword, not yet drawn.

Damas.name: Damas
Damas.biography: Roger de Damas, reorganizer of the Bourbon army - Naples plays its double game, a neutrality treaty in one hand and the Coalition's promises in the other.

Frederick.name: Frederick
Frederick.biography: Crown Prince Frederick, regent of Denmark - the army concentrated in Holstein, guarding an armed neutrality.

Castanos.name: Castanos
Castanos.biography: Castanos, Commandant-General of the Campo de Gibraltar - Spain's war with Britain is fought at sea; Trafalgar is four weeks out.

Abdurrahman.name: Abdurrahman
Abdurrahman.biography: Kadi Abdurrahman Pasha, governor of Karaman, with the Nizam-i Cedid new-model troops - the Porte's reformed army, far from Europe's quarrel.

Dumonceau.name: Dumonceau
Dumonceau.biography: Jean-Baptiste Dumonceau - a Brussels-born general of the Batavian army; his Dutch division marched with Marmont's corps to the Danube in 1805.

Teulie.name: Teulie
Teulie.biography: Pietro Teulie - Milanese patriot and minister of war; he led the Italian division north with the Grande Armee in 1805 and fell before Kolberg in 1807.

Paget.name: Paget
Paget.biography: Henry Paget - the finest cavalry officer Britain owns, and the boldest. His charges end in glory or in Spain.

Bennigsen.name: Bennigsen
Bennigsen.biography: Levin von Bennigsen - the stubborn Hanoverian in Russian service. Unlovable, unbreakable, and unforgiving of rivals.

pending_marshal_petition.title: Marshal Massena seeks an audience
pending_marshal_petition.body: Sire, Massena has expressed... displeasure about Ney's recent recognition. He requests a command worthy of his talents.
pending_marshal_petition.speaker: Massena
pending_marshal_petition.speaker_line: "Sire — I have earned better than to watch Ney take the field while I hold a road."

options.label: Let it stand
options.detail: Free, and it fixes nothing. For 3 more turns he brings NONE of his 17,711 men to any battle Ney leads, and the quarrel may harden further.

options.label: Promise Glory
options.detail: His patience is bought — the grievance shortens by 2 turns, and for 6 turns the quarrel cannot harden further.

options.label: Rebuke
options.detail: Trust -5. The grievance shortens by 1 turn. He will not act on his own this cycle — he respects the Emperor's anger, briefly.

options.label: Give him a command
options.detail: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.
options.unavailable_reason: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.

event_log.enemy_voice: Archduke Charles: "France pays full price for every Austrian mile now."

event_log.message: Supply shortage at Tyrol: Archduke Charles loses 1,464 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Archduke John loses 593 troops
Holland sends 6,500 men under Dumonceau to the colours at Amsterdam — they await the orders of France. The nearest host is Davout at Rhineland. Holland pays them; their dead will be its grief.
The Kingdom of Italy sends 7,500 men under Teulie to the colours at Milan — they await the orders of France. They stand with Massena. The Kingdom of Italy pays them; their dead will be its grief.

event_log.enemy_voice: Mack: "This is not a rout. It is a revision of the plan."

event_log.battle_name: The Great Second Battle of Milan
event_log.enemy_voice: Archduke Charles: "Your Emperor needs quick victories. I need only deny them."
Archduke Charles: "The moment was measured twice before I struck."

event_log.message: Supply shortage at Franconia: Ney loses 480 troops
Supply shortage at Franconia: Davout loses 514 troops
Supply shortage at Franconia: Bernadotte loses 358 troops
Crowded at Swabia: Lannes loses 345 troops to the press of 3 corps on one province's roads
Crowded at Swabia: Murat loses 421 troops to the press of 3 corps on one province's roads
Crowded at Swabia: Napoleon loses 187 troops to the press of 3 corps on one province's roads
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Mack loses 807 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Archduke Charles loses 1,804 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Archduke John loses 858 troops

event_log.enemy_voice: Archduke John: "Neither yields. The Alps are patient, and so am I."
Mack: "The army retires; the system remains intact. You will see."

event_log.battle_name: The Great Third Battle of Tyrol
event_log.enemy_voice: Archduke Charles: "Patience wins wars, not charges."
Archduke Charles: "You were overextended. I merely presented the invoice."
Archduke John: "I attack only when the ledger favors it. It did."

event_log.message: Supply shortage at Tyrol: Ney loses 470 troops — 81 of them to living off the land (this stripped country feeds a French army 80%)
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Archduke Charles loses 810 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Archduke John loses 332 troops

event_log.battle_name: The Great Sixth Battle of Tyrol
event_log.enemy_voice: Archduke Charles: "I spend ground as a miser spends coin — rarely, and never twice."
Archduke Charles: "We will meet again on ground of my choosing."
Archduke Charles: "Austria endures. It is the thing we do best."

event_log.message: Supply shortage at Volhynia: Kutuzov loses 411 troops
Supply shortage at Volhynia: Buxhowden loses 376 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Ney loses 422 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Davout loses 1,158 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Massena loses 1,204 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Napoleon loses 437 troops
Supply shortage at Tyrol: Teulie loses 268 troops
Prussia will move on Hanover — The Hanoverian Prize. You may compensate (1,200g — you can afford it); guarantee Hanover (1 DP — 7 in hand); or let the war come, having been asked.

event_log.enemy_voice: Archduke Charles: "An army preserved is a battle not yet lost."

event_log.message: The Archduke Charles has been CAPTURED by France at Bohemia.
The Archduke John's corps has been destroyed at Bohemia

event_log.enemy_voice: Mack: "Withdrawal conducted in order. The army is intact."

event_log.message: Crowded at Bohemia: Ney loses 246 troops to the press of 5 corps on one province's roads
Crowded at Bohemia: Davout loses 712 troops to the press of 5 corps on one province's roads
Crowded at Bohemia: Massena loses 708 troops to the press of 5 corps on one province's roads
Crowded at Bohemia: Napoleon loses 273 troops to the press of 5 corps on one province's roads
Crowded at Bohemia: Teulie loses 165 troops to the press of 5 corps on one province's roads
Prussia delivers a final demand to Hanover — it is refused.

event_log.author: France
event_log.message: Austria swears revanche — the court will not forgive France the loss of Bohemia and 1 more province.

gazette_issues.lead: VICTOIRE! The Emperor himself carries the day at Swabia — France has seen his genius with her own eyes.
war: The Great Battle of Tyrol: Ney (France) attacked Archduke John (Austria) — stalemate (6,692 / 6,252 casualties) — Archduke John: "Neither yields. The Alps are patient, and so am I."
Second Battle of Tyrol: Ney (France) attacked Mack (Austria) — Ney tactical victory (1,980 / 6,243 casualties) — Mack: "The army retires; the system remains intact. You will see."
The Great Third Battle of Tyrol: Massena (France) attacked Archduke Charles (Austria) — stalemate (6,511 / 5,946 casualties) — Archduke Charles: "Patience wins wars, not charges."

Fourth Battle of Tyrol: Archduke Charles (Austria) attacked Ney (France) — Archduke Charles tactical victory (2,252 / 3,498 casualties) — Archduke Charles: "You were overextended. I merely presented the invoice."
Fifth Battle of Tyrol: Archduke John (Austria) attacked Ney (France) — Archduke John tactical victory (1,782 / 3,183 casualties) — Archduke John: "I attack only when the ledger favors it. It did."

The Great Sixth Battle of Tyrol: Ney (France) attacked Archduke Charles (Austria) — Ney tactical victory (4,116 / 7,032 casualties) — Archduke Charles: "I spend ground as a miser spends coin — rarely, and never twice."
Seventh Battle of Tyrol: Ney (France) attacked Archduke Charles (Austria) — Ney tactical victory (3,242 / 5,831 casualties) — Archduke Charles: "We will meet again on ground of my choosing."
Eighth Battle of Tyrol: Ney (France) attacked Archduke Charles (Austria) — Ney tactical victory (2,270 / 5,510 casualties) — Archduke Charles: "Austria endures. It is the thing we do best."
army: General Mack WOUNDED at Bohemia — out until turn 6; the corps stands
Ney (France) stands crowned with glory — the army's most celebrated commander
gazette_issues.bourse: THE BOURSE — The English squadrons press our trade; the Treasury stands at 2,959 francs and the merchants grumble.

turn_events.message: Supply cost you 2,104 men, at Bohemia.
Berthier notes that Bernadotte no longer presses the matter — his quarrel with Ney has cooled.
Bernadotte's resentment of Ney has cooled with time.
Berthier reports that Massena appears envious of Ney's laurels — he has grown restless for glory.
Massena seeks an audience, Sire — his card waits on the Generals screen and on the rail.

headline.text: Sire — the Archduke John of Austria is destroyed at Bohemia — his corps annihilated, his name struck from their order of battle.
sub_beats: Sire — the Archduke Charles of Austria is taken at Bohemia — he is our prisoner, and their order of battle is one commander shorter.
Sire — Marshal Ney has destroyed Archduke John's corps at Bohemia. No enemy formation remains in that field.

last_morning_dispatch.berthier_note: Their order of battle is one commander shorter — permanently, Sire. Press the advantage while their line is headless.

congress_clock.line: THE CONGRESS OF PARIS — 35 of 45 titled (2 held, unsettled: Bohemia, Tyrol) · summon from the Cabinet (F1)

held_roads.text: Bohemia — a peace with Austria that leaves it ours titles it at the signature; otherwise 12 quiet turns from the peace
held_roads.short: Bohemia needs a peace with Austria

held_roads.text: Tyrol — a peace with Austria that leaves it ours titles it at the signature; otherwise 12 quiet turns from the peace
held_roads.short: Tyrol needs a peace with Austria

unmarched.text: Britain has no road to us but the sea, and Normandy is a defended shore: she can land only by expedition, 15,000 men at a time.
Russia's straight road to us is closed — the neutrality of Saxony bars it; the lawful road is 3 marches.

war_objectives.text: War Purpose: Defense vs Britain — the homeland — 28 of 28 provinces held  |  Settlement: White Peace (-2)
War Purpose: Defense vs Austria — the homeland — 28 of 28 provinces held  |  Settlement: Dictated Terms (+54)
War Purpose: Defense vs Russia — the homeland — 28 of 28 provinces held  |  Settlement: White Peace (+0)

diplomatic_events.text: THE LANDING: Paget has put 5,000 men ashore at Lisbon.
THE LAWS: Prussia enacts the Articles of War — infantry drafts muster at +10 morale; cures Brittle — the court's doctrine flaw — while its Staff stands.
Talleyrand reports: 7 diplomatic points available (base 3, +1 skill, +1 authority, +2 carried from last turn).
An envoy from the Kingdom of Italy has arrived with a petition.
Britain's gold reaches Austria — the subsidy stands at 300 this season.
Prussia delivers a final demand to Hanover — it is refused. The ladder has one rung left.
REVANCHE: Austria will not forgive France the loss of Bohemia and 1 more province. A new design hardens in their court.
The court of Austria takes up a new design: Revanche.

France.name: Talleyrand
France.biography: The devil's diplomat. Serves France — or rather, serves what he believes France should be.

Britain.name: Castlereagh
Britain.biography: Cold, calculating, implacable. Views any French advantage as a threat to the balance of power.

Russia.name: Czartoryski
Russia.biography: Alexander's foreign minister; dreams of a Europe re-drawn to Russian design.

Spain.name: Cevallos
Spain.biography: Godoy's man at the ministry; binds Spain to the French star for now.

Ottoman.name: Reis Efendi
Ottoman.biography: The Porte's chief scribe of foreign affairs; patient, evasive, immovable.

Sweden.name: Ehrenheim
Sweden.biography: Serves a king whose loathing of Bonaparte outruns Sweden's means.

Naples.name: Medici
Naples.biography: Steers the Bourbon court between the French army and the British fleet.

Portugal.name: Araujo
Portugal.biography: Keeps Lisbon's old alliance with London alive without provoking Madrid.

Denmark.name: Bernstorff
Denmark.biography: Guards Danish neutrality and the Sound, wary of every fleet that nears it.

Bavaria.name: Montgelas
Bavaria.biography: Architect of a modern Bavaria; casts his lot with Paris to grow it.

Hanover.name: Chancery of Hanover
Hanover.biography: An electorate that shares Britain's crown and France's occupation both.

Hesse.name: Chancery of Hesse
Hesse.biography: A small German court trying to stay small and unnoticed.

PapalStates.name: Consalvi
PapalStates.biography: Cardinal Secretary of State; defends the Church's temporal remnant with guile.

Sardinia.name: Chancery of Sardinia
Sardinia.biography: A king exiled to his island, waiting for Piedmont's return.

Holland.name: Schimmelpenninck
Holland.biography: Grand Pensionary of a republic that lives on French sufferance.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Marescalchi
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Foreign minister of a kingdom whose king wears the French crown.

Switzerland.name: Chancery of Helvetia
Switzerland.biography: Confederate cantons mediated — in every sense — by Bonaparte.

current.talleyrand_text:
Sire, Marescalchi brings a petition from the Kingdom of Italy. The Kingdom of Italy petitions the Emperor for a province.

  Grant it, and Tyrol passes to the Kingdom of Italy: loyalty +0 (its loyalty is already full), its bond with us rises 0 → 20 (worth +1 a turn in loyalty, now +0), for 1 DP. Our net rises by 47g a turn — 20g of income forfeited, 52g of occupation relieved, 15g returned as tribute at today's 75% rate, the force limit falls 2,500 at no cost today.
  Refuse it, and the Kingdom of Italy loses 10 loyalty and its bond with us falls 20 (0 → -20: worth -1 a turn in loyalty, now +0); nothing is charged.
  Left unanswered at the turn's end, the petition lapses — and a lapse is a refusal.

Talleyrand: "A client that asks for land still counts itself ours, Sire. Grant it and the bond deepens; refuse it and the standing it spent to ask does not return."
